source_caption:
Jim Carrey's manic, genre-defining performance in Me, Myself & Irene relies heavily on his ability to shift between the mild-mannered Charlie and the aggressive Hank. It also cemented the film as a commercial success, grossing nearly $149.3 million worldwide.

Directors ⁠Bobby Farrelly and Peter Farrelly knew that Carrey thrived on pushing boundaries, so they routinely kept cameras rolling long after the scripted dialogue ended. This freedom allowed Carrey to heavily improvise, leading to unscripted, highly authentic reactions from co-star ⁠Renée Zellweger during key sequences. He famously began practicing his rubbery, "elastic" facial control in the mirror early in his career, an expert skill he utilizes extensively to visually distinguish his two warring personalities, the submissive Charlie and the menacing Hank.

source_details.title: Me, Myself & Irene
source_details.synopsis: Me, Myself & Irene is a 2000 American slapstick black comedy film produced, co-written, and directed by the Farrelly brothers, and starring Jim Carrey and Renée Zellweger. The film centers around a Rhode Island state trooper named Charlie (Carrey) who, after years of continuously suppressing his feelings, suffers a psychotic breakdown that results in a second personality, Hank, and must deal with his newfound condition while escorting a woman named Irene (Zellweger) who is being hunted by her mob-affiliated ex-boyfriend.
